title: dedicated-autoscaler-priority-scheduling-burst-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Maya Chen
body:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets with mixed customer priority tiers occasionally experience burst token starvation for high-priority tenants under transient load spikes. This leads to tail-latency SLO regressions even though aggregate utilization appears healthy. This PR implements a priority-aware scheduling enhancement and richer utilization/burst reporting so operators can observe per-priority token consumption and tune smoothing/limits.

What this PR does (single run-on description): Adds per-priority token-bucket accounting in the dedicated autoscaler, introduces a smoothing window for burst depletion to avoid hard preemption during short spikes, exposes new Prometheus metrics for per-fleet and per-priority burst and tokenbucket state, updates the autoscaler config schema to allow per-priority burst limits and smoothing params, adds dashboards and alerting panels to Grafana JSON for utilization and burst anomalies, includes unit/integration tests that simulate multi-priority traffic bursts, and provides a migration path for existing fleet configs so default behavior remains unchanged.

Design notes: The autoscaler now maintains lightweight token-bucket state keyed by (fleet_id, priority). A smoothing window (configurable, default 60s) computes an exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) of recent burst consumption to decide whether to allow short bursts above steady throughput. A hard cap still prevents unbounded bursts. Metrics added: redwood_autoscaler_burst_tokens_available{fleet,priority}, redwood_autoscaler_burst_tokens_consumed_total{fleet,priority}, redwood_autoscaler_burst_ewma_consumption{fleet,priority,window}, redwood_autoscaler_priority_prefill{fleet,priority}. We also add redwood_autoscaler_backpressure_events_total{fleet,priority} to help correlate SLO events.

Config: schema change in pkg/config/autoscaler_schema.go; YAML example in docs/configs/dedicated-autoscaler.md shows new fields under "burst_policy.priority_overrides" with per-priority "max_tokens", "refill_rate", and "smoothing_window_sec". Defaults preserve previous behavior (single global token bucket) when priority_overrides is omitted.

Testing: Unit tests for token-bucket logic and EWMA in autoscaler/tokenbucket_test.go. Integration test harness in perf-canary/test-fixtures spins up a small dedicated-like cluster and replays synthetic multi-priority traces to validate that high-priority tail latency improves while overall throughput stays within SLA. CI: full unit + integration suite passed locally and in CI.

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind config flag "enable_priority_burst_policy" (default false). We will roll out to canary fleet, monitor new metrics and backpressure alerts for one week, then enable by default for dedicated fleets with >X qps.

Release notes: Added priority-aware burst controls and utilization reporting to the dedicated autoscaler. Operators can now set per-priority burst limits and smoothing windows, and will gain visibility into per-priority token consumption and backpressure events.
commits: feat(autoscaler): add per-priority token-bucket accounting and smoothing window
chore(config): extend autoscaler schema with priority_overrides and docs example
feat(metrics): export per-priority burst & backpressure Prometheus metrics
test(autoscaler): unit tests for token bucket and EWMA smoothing
test(integration): canary harness scenarios for multi-priority bursts
docs: update dedicated-autoscaler config and runbook
perf: micro-optimizations in token bucket path to reduce allocations
changed_files: services/autoscaler/priority_bucket.go (new): implements per-priority token buckets and EWMA smoothing
services/autoscaler/scheduler.go: integrate priority-aware admission checks and backpressure logging
pkg/config/autoscaler_schema.go: add priority_overrides fields and validation
docs/configs/dedicated-autoscaler.md: YAML examples and migration notes
review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Could you clarify the cost implications of tracking per-priority buckets at scale? Concerned about memory growth for fleets with many priorities.

Maya Chen: We shard buckets by active priorities and expire idle entries after 10m of inactivity; memory overhead measured in benchmarks is ~120 bytes per active priority per fleet. Added comments and an LRU-like eviction in priority_bucket.go.
Priya Rao: Tests look good; can we add a deterministic test for the smoothing EWMA seeds so regression binaries produce stable metrics?
Maya Chen: Added deterministic seeding and an explicit test case (tokenbucket_test.go) that validates EWMA behavior against expected values.
Diego Marquez: Observability LGTM; suggest adding an alert query for sustained depletion (tokens_available < 10% for 2 windows).
Maya Chen: Added recommended alert to dashboards JSON and included it in the runbook section of dedicated-autoscaler.md.
notes_for_ops:
Migration: existing fleets unchanged unless priority_overrides is configured or enable_priority_burst_policy is enabled. When enabling feature gate, monitor redwood_autoscaler_burst_tokens_consumed_total and redwood_autoscaler_backpressure_events_total across fleets. Recommended conservative defaults: max_tokens: 2000, refill_rate: 50/s, smoothing_window_sec: 60.

Runbook excerpt: If high-priority backpressure events spike after enabling, temporarily increase max_tokens for affected priority or increase smoothing_window_sec, then investigate long-tail request patterns and consider autoscaler throughput adjustments.
release_notes: Added per-priority burst controls: configure per-priority max_tokens, refill_rate, and smoothing_window_sec.
Exported Prometheus metrics for per-priority burst tokens and backpressure events.
New Grafana dashboard panels and recommended alerting rules for burst/utilization anomalies.
Feature gated behind enable_priority_burst_policy (off by default).
